newsitem.title: UK: Softs Outlook-Consolidation likely, markets eye US.
newsitem.headline: Softs Outlook-Consolidation likely, markets eye US.

text.p: Soft commodity markets are expected to hold in last week's ranges until fresh news emerges or U.S. markets break out of their current ranges, traders said on Monday.
The sterling-denominated cocoa market was expected to consolidate for the time being, with traders seeing few fundamental reasons for prices to move either up or down.
Technically the market might find more room to rebound after last week's sharp sell-off. "But apart from the technical side, there are no fundamental factors for the rise," said one.

Resistance for benchmark September was pegged at 1,000 stg a tonne, followed by a small chart gap between 1,012 and 1,015 stg. Initial support was seen at a gap between 939 and 949 once the immediate floor at 965 was taken out.
Traders said the market was still vulnerable to long liquidation from speculators.

On the fundamental front, the market's immediate concern was the onset of the main 1997/98 cocoa crop in Ivory Coast. The crop was believed to be developing well with the preliminary estimate pegged at just over 1.0 million tonnes.
Analysts say the El Nino weather system was not expected to impact world markets for the next eight months or so.
"Traditionally, the market never rallies at this time of the year as there's going to be ample cocoa," one trader said, adding that manufacturers would have adequate supplies.
In robusta coffee, traders said the market could consolidate at its current levels after the recent sharp falls, although some suggested that the short-term direction was still unclear.

Others said prices could try to make further upside headway despite the lack of traded volume. One positive factor was the possible turnaround in the New York market, which could boost London sentiment, they said.
"London will remain locked in a sideways to upward move," said one trader. "It has seen its lows in the short term." Last week, benchmark September sank to a six-month low of $1,477.
Support for September was placed at $1,545 with the nearby upside target at $1,645, and then $1,700. "But there's plenty of overhead resistance beyond $1,645," the trader said.
In white sugar, traders said London was likely to wait until the New York raws market broke out of its current range-bound activity.

"People are sitting back for the time being seeing how the dust settles," said one trader, referring to last week's fund buying, which drove benchmark October to a new life of contract high of $330.20.
Although the increased speculator position had been a talking point in London, the main focus of interest would be the New York stand-off between fund buyers and trade and producer sellers.
"London is hanging onto the tails of whatever New York does at the moment, there doesn't appear to be any real movement going on in the whites," the trader said.
Continued talk of Russian buying interest in whites -- Baltic ports were rumoured to have taken in at least 30,000 tonnes recently -- had kept London supported in recent days.
